open_points.subject: all refusals
open_points.text: “a bounded reason naming the first failing check” and “it is not a machine identifier, and no caller branches on it … reasons are not [closed]”
open_points.question: What exact, stable reason text must each refusal return, including how fields and record identities are rendered?
options: Define one template for every failing check
Allow arbitrary bounded human-readable wording
open_points.default_guess: Use stable templates keyed by the failed check, with canonical field and identity rendering.

open_points.subject: surface field-size validation
open_points.text: “a value of a trial case or constant, at most stored_value_bytes_max … every other string anywhere in the request, at most bounded_text_bytes_max”
open_points.question: Does bounded_text_bytes_max apply to strings nested inside JSON values and schemas, or only to standalone textual fields such as names and purposes?
options: Apply it to every nested JSON string
Apply it only to standalone text fields; bound values and schemas as wholes
open_points.default_guess: Apply it only to standalone text fields, not strings inside an otherwise bounded value or schema.

open_points.subject: surface request-size validation
open_points.text: “its size, counted as the bytes of the request message as received”
open_points.question: Which bytes count toward surface_request_bytes_max: the MCP payload, its serialized JSON-RPC envelope, or transport framing as well?
options: Count the complete serialized MCP/JSON-RPC message excluding transport framing
Count only operation arguments
Count transport framing too
open_points.default_guess: Count the complete serialized MCP/JSON-RPC message excluding transport framing.

open_points.subject: store.open_store privacy checks
open_points.text: “private directory” and “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user”
open_points.question: What exact ownership and permission checks define a private data directory and private existing contents?
options: Require ownership by the kernel UID and no group/other permission bits
Require mode 0700 for directories and 0600 for files
Check only the top-level directory
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group or other permissions on the directory and every existing entry.

open_points.subject: manifest JSON parsing
open_points.text: “the service record … is not valid JSON” and “record_digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of that one capability entry”
open_points.question: Are duplicate object member names in a manifest record invalid, and if so at which manifest check are they reported?
options: Reject every duplicate member as invalid JSON
Use the parser's last value
Reject duplicates only inside the capability entry being digested
open_points.default_guess: Reject duplicate members anywhere in the record as invalid JSON.

open_points.subject: installation JSON parsing
open_points.text: “one JSON object with exactly the installation's fields”
open_points.question: Are duplicate object member names in the installation file invalid, including duplicates of scalar fields such as owner_token or manifest_revision?
options: Reject every duplicate member
Use the parser's last value
Only detect duplicate services and agent names explicitly listed
open_points.default_guess: Reject every duplicate member during parsing.

open_points.subject: manifest revision access
open_points.text: “reads a service's record only from <manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured manifest_revision”
open_points.question: How does bindings obtain the file at manifest_revision: from a Git object, a revision-named snapshot directory, or an already checked-out tree whose revision is merely asserted?
options: Read the file from a Git tree at the named revision
Treat manifest_location as an immutable snapshot already corresponding to the revision
Use a revision-named subdirectory
open_points.default_guess: Read the file directly from the repository tree object at the configured revision.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances
open_points.text: “an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service”
open_points.question: Which A08 rule 5 checks are “of the record itself” at startup, when no operation name or proposed ports are available?
options: Check only top-level service/capabilities structure and duplicate capability names
Validate every capability entry completely
Check only the selected instance and its required headers
open_points.default_guess: Check top-level service identity, capabilities structure and duplicate capability names, then the selected instance fields needed for the header-collision check.

open_points.subject: service api_base_url
open_points.text: “an absolute http or https URL with a host” and “the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path”
open_points.question: May api_base_url contain user information, a query, fragment, or non-root path, and does “without a trailing /” remove one slash or all trailing slashes?
options: Allow only scheme, authority and an optional path; reject userinfo, query and fragment
Allow every syntactically absolute HTTP URL and apply generic URL resolution
Require a scheme and authority only
open_points.default_guess: Reject userinfo, query and fragment; allow a path prefix and remove all trailing slashes before appending the declared path.

open_points.subject: plain HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: “or one whose api_base_url host is a loopback address”
open_points.question: Does the exception require a literal loopback IP address, or may a hostname such as localhost qualify after DNS resolution?
options: Only a literal IP in a loopback range qualifies
A hostname qualifies when every resolved address is loopback
A hostname qualifies when any resolved address is loopback
open_points.default_guess: Require a literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback address.

open_points.subject: HTTPS verification
open_points.text: “TLS is verified for https”
open_points.question: Which trust roots, hostname rules and client TLS settings define successful verification?
options: Use the host system trust store and standard hostname verification
Ship release-pinned trust roots
Require installation-provided trust roots
open_points.default_guess: Use the host system trust store with standard hostname verification and no custom override.

open_points.subject: HTTP connection attempts
open_points.text: “nothing is retried inside one attempt” and “An invocation is one HTTP request”
open_points.question: May the HTTP client try another resolved address after a connection failure before any request byte is written, or does that count as a forbidden retry?
options: Try only one resolved address
Allow address fallback until the first request byte is written
Allow the HTTP library's default address fallback
open_points.default_guess: Allow address fallback before any request byte is written, but never repeat a request after writing begins.

open_points.subject: credential decoding
open_points.text: “decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline” and “holds … a control character”
open_points.question: Does one trailing newline mean LF only or CRLF as one newline, and which Unicode characters count as control characters?
options: Strip one LF and an immediately preceding CR; reject Unicode control categories
Strip only one LF; reject ASCII C0 and DEL
Strip any terminal line ending; reject C0, DEL and C1
open_points.default_guess: Strip one terminal LF with an optional preceding CR, and reject C0, DEL and C1 control characters.

open_points.subject: service request shape for path placeholders
open_points.text: “every {name} of the path is an input port whose schema's type is string or integer”
open_points.question: Must a path-placeholder input also have value carriage and cardinality one, or may a file or many port pass proposal checks and fail every invocation as input_not_placeable?
options: Require value carriage and cardinality one at binding proposal
Allow other carriage/cardinality and fail at send time
open_points.default_guess: Require a one-cardinality value input at proposal time.

open_points.subject: flow and binding port schemas
open_points.text: M01 says a value_schema is “written in the subset of JSON Schema the kernel supports”, while A05 rule 7 does not list unsupported flow-port or constant schemas and A08 only names some applicable A02 port rules
open_points.question: Which operation rejects an unsupported schema on a flow port, flow constant or binding port, with which refusal and at what position in its check order?
options: Reject it during composition or binding proposal before identity is recorded
Keep the flow and report it as a proof failure
Allow it until a runtime fit is attempted
open_points.default_guess: Reject unsupported schemas during composition or binding proposal, before recording anything, in port-name order.

open_points.subject: sandbox non-canonical outputs
open_points.text: “The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every value output” and canonical_bytes “refuse[s] a value JCS cannot represent”
open_points.question: What sandbox outcome is produced when run returns a value such as NaN, infinity, a set, or another object that cannot be represented as canonical JSON?
options: contract_violation
crashed
sandbox_violation
open_points.default_guess: Classify it as contract_violation with no output stored.

open_points.subject: mapped element identity
open_points.text: “map_index” is used throughout, but only list_index is explicitly said to start “from 0”
open_points.question: What map_index is assigned to the first and subsequent elements of a mapped node?
options: Zero-based list index
One-based ordinal
open_points.default_guess: Use the zero-based list index.

open_points.subject: effect approval for file inputs
open_points.text: State 0 says multipart “parts themselves — name, filename, media type and content — are what the owner was shown”, while A10 says the preview carries “for each file input, its digest, size and media type” and the request description carries “the SHA-256 of its content”
open_points.question: Does an approval response show the owner the actual file bytes, or only their digest, size, media type and separately readable spool identity?
options: Include the file bytes in the approval preview
Include only file facts and require optional read_spooled_file inspection
Include a bounded preview plus digest
open_points.default_guess: Include only file facts and the spooled-file identity; the owner reads the complete bytes separately when desired.

open_points.subject: operation_failed diagnostics
open_points.text: “Details of an element that concluded operation_failed … are a closed set” while A09 says an unused response body may be kept as failure_detail, and M23 names only failure_detail; send_prepared_request separately returns a detail code and a bounded failure_detail
open_points.question: Where is the closed operation_failed detail code persisted and returned when a response body also supplies failure_detail?
options: Add a separate detail_code field to NodeExecution
Store only the detail code and discard the body detail
Encode both into the one failure_detail text
open_points.default_guess: Persist a separate detail_code and keep failure_detail for the bounded diagnostic body.

open_points.subject: masked failure details
open_points.text: “a classified failure_detail [is returned as] its length and class”
open_points.question: Is the reported length a Unicode code-point count, UTF-8 byte count before truncation, or UTF-8 byte count of the retained bounded detail?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the retained detail
Unicode code points of the retained detail
Original body or exception-message byte length before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the retained, already bounded failure_detail.

open_points.subject: sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”, while A03 permits opening paths inside “the exchange directory and the read-only runtime”
open_points.question: May agent code itself read arbitrary runtime files and create arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or are those paths available only to the sandbox runner for input/output transfer?
options: Permit user code to access both allowed trees
Permit runtime reads but restrict exchange access to declared inputs and outputs
Deny user open calls entirely and let only the runner access those paths
open_points.default_guess: Permit runtime reads and exchange-directory access as the more specific A03 rule states.

open_points.subject: sandbox process_count
open_points.text: “process_count” and “setrlimit (address space, processes)”
open_points.question: Does process_count include the initial Python runner, only child processes, or every process visible under the sandbox UID, and what exact event counts as hitting the limit?
options: Count the runner and all descendants
Count only descendants created by the implementation
Use the host RLIMIT_NPROC result without translating its scope
open_points.default_guess: Count the runner and all descendants inside the isolated environment.

open_points.subject: sandbox failure_detail
open_points.text: “only for the exception type and message”
open_points.question: What exact text is recorded for an exception, including qualification of the type, separator, empty messages and nested exception chains?
options: Stable '<type>: <message>' using the unqualified type name and no chain
Use Python's default exception formatting
Record type and message as separate structured fields
open_points.default_guess: Use a stable unqualified type name followed by ': ' and the message, omitting the separator for an empty message and omitting chains.

open_points.subject: HTTP response validity
open_points.text: “a malformed status line or headers” and “no valid final response received”
open_points.question: Which HTTP grammar violations, duplicate headers other than Content-Type, obsolete folding and conflicting framing headers make a response malformed?
options: Apply a named strict RFC 9110/9112 profile
Use the pinned HTTP library's acceptance rules
List kernel-specific accepted and rejected forms
open_points.default_guess: Apply a strict RFC 9110/9112 profile and reject obsolete folding, invalid field syntax and conflicting framing.
